Expected variable labels from a PV

Source: R/labels.R
pv_var_labels.Rd

Derives the variable label that each variable should have in the field data from the va- and vb-tags of a PV. Items whose va-tag holds several variables, e.g. dates (etstdat (etstm / etstj)), multiple choice items (ts2352 (ts23525 / ts23526 / ...)) or lists separated by commas (h_etzeit (h_etzeit1, h_etzeit2, ...)), are split into one row per variable.

Usage

pv_var_labels(pv)

Arguments

pv

The result of read_pv(), or a path (or several paths) to PV docx files.

Value

A data frame with one row per variable and the columns var, label (expected label), item, va, vb, pv and note.

Details

The labels in the data are built by the survey institute from the vb-tag. Brackets and slashes are dropped and every variable of a grouped item gets the text of the vb-tag with its own part of the list, e.g.

  • etstm from vb "Startdatum (-monat/-jahr) Erwerbsepisode" becomes "Startdatum Monat Erwerbsepisode"

  • etintro1a1 from vb "Interviewerangabe bei Widerspruch (Berufsangabe / Berufsartangabe / Zeitpunkt)" becomes "Interviewerangabe bei Widerspruch Berufsangabe"

  • h_etzeit1 from vb "Zeitarbeit andauernder Erwerbsepisoden (h_etzeit1, h_etzeit2, ...)" becomes "Zeitarbeit andauernder Erwerbsepisoden h_etzeit1"

The list in the vb-tag is the first bracket with slashes or commas whose number of parts equals the number of variables in the va-tag (or, if there is none, the first bracket with slashes or commas). The parts are assigned to the variables in order. If the va-tag holds more variables than the list has parts, which is common for multiple choice items whose last variables stand for refusal and don't know, the label of the remaining variables is taken from their line in the we-tag (e.g. the line ts23528: verweigert gives the text of the vb-tag before the list followed by "verweigert"). Every such case is mentioned in note. If no label can be derived, label is NA and note says why.

Markers in front of the variable name (e.g. [ZS], [HILF]) and [MF] at the start of the vb-tag are removed.

See also

label_test(), which uses this function. Call it yourself (nepstest:::pv_var_labels()) to see which label a variable is expected to have.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
labels <- nepstest:::pv_var_labels("NEPS_B180_SC6_EP_26ET_V2_2_20250312.docx")
labels[labels$var %in% c("etstm", "ts23528"), ]
} # }
